title: Frictionless Savings Program — roadmap, milestone map, and governance charter
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Create a tracked initiative that coordinates product, design, and engineering work to realize measurable token-cost savings via three levers: adaptive batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles. Deliverables: milestone map, per-lever success metrics, rollout governance, experiment registry, and an ops dashboard (health + signal taxonomy) for auto-rollout/rollback decisions.
objectives: Reduce hosted per-token cost by 15% (primary OKR) while keeping P99 latency SLOs stable
Create an experiment and rollout governance playbook so any rollout has a clear abort criterion and duration
Ship a single-pane Savings Ops dashboard with daily drift alerts and per-model savings attribution
milestones: M2: Engineering spike + baseline telemetry capture (in progress) — end 2026-03-15
M3: Field experiments for batching & cache (runbook + infra) — 2026-04-15
M4: Quantization profiles validated on 3 representative models — 2026-05-20
M5: Ops dashboard v1 + canary rollout of knobs (10% traffic) — 2026-06-10
M6: Full rollout + post-rollout regression check & retrospective — 2026-06-30
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment produces statistically significant cost reduction vs. baseline (p<0.05)
SLO guardrails: no increase >5% in tail latency (P99) for canary traffic
Playbook documents runbook steps, rollback triggers, owner list, and monitoring links
Savings Ops dashboard shows per-model token cost delta and can show attribution between batching/caching/quantization
decisions: Adopt a conservative default: enable KV cache + small batching for low-risk traffic first
Preferred metric for rollout decisions: 7-day rolling token-cost-per-1M and P99 latency delta
Use staged quantization (int8 -> int4 if available) behind feature flags with model-specific guardrails
Governance: PM owns rollout window & success criteria; Eng owns runbook and kill-switch; DX owns dashboard signals
